title: cli: `os build` / `os validate` report a permission-set name collision — the compile door for #17516
body:
Fixes #18024

Clause-②: no — this card adds NO published export and re-stamps no error-code vocabulary. It consumes exports `@objectstack/plugin-security` already publishes (that is why PR #18022 itself graded `yes`/`minor`), and making an existing refusal visible is a tightening or neutral, never a widening of an accept set. The `dispatcher-error-vocabulary` token stays stamped `event`, untouched: this change creates no stamp site at all. Both of the card's stated flip conditions were checked against the delivered diff and neither holds.

## What this is

PR #18022 (card #17516) gave the permission-set **name-collision** refusal a **runtime** door. The **compile-time** door was missing: `os build` and `os validate` walked an artifact in which two packages declare the same permission-set name and said nothing, so the first an author heard of an entire declared set never materializing was a boot warning on a deployed environment.

#14553 set the shape for exactly this on `navigationContributions` — the same finding raised at **both** doors, behind **one** shared predicate so the two cannot drift. Its compile half is `packages/cli/src/utils/nav-contribution-groups.ts`; this change is the same half for permission sets.

## What it does NOT do

- ⛔ **The skip is unchanged.** Refusing to write into a row another package owns is correct under ADR-0086 D4. Only its VISIBILITY was at issue.
- ⛔ **It reports; it never refuses.** `severity: 'warning'` is declared at the producer and the failure direction is CLOSED — the set is not installed, so nothing is over-granted. This follows what #14553 chose for nav (the maintainer's option B) rather than departing from it; making either command exit non-zero would narrow what `os build` accepts, which is a different decision from the one this card carries.
- ⛔ **No new payload key.** The findings ride the `warnings` key both `os build --json` and `os validate --json` already declare — the shape `build-json-advisory-parity` and `build-json-undeclared-key-parity` pin by name. Both commands compute the list, so the residue pin ("nothing rides in build that validate does not also report") holds rather than being weakened to fit.
- ⚠️ **`os validate --strict` does promote them**, as it promotes every other member of `warnings` — that is the declared meaning of the flag (*"Treat warnings as errors"*), and the nav half has had the same property since #14553. Neither command's DEFAULT accept set changes.

## ⭐ One derivation, consumed — not re-derived

`packages/cli/src/utils/permission-set-name-collisions.ts` imports the predicate and the wording from `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s package entry, where #17516 published them for this consumer:

- the owner comparison is `permissionSetNameIsForeign` — ⛔ never a local comparison, because a nullish owner is FOREIGN by that function's ruling;
- the sentence is `permissionSetNameCollisionDiagnostic` + `formatPermissionSetNameCollisionDiagnostic` — ⛔ never retyped, because two doors phrasing one refusal differently IS the defect.

`reportPermissionSetNameCollisions` is deliberately NOT consumed, and the bound is stated in the module header: it is a sink-printing pass reporter whose sentence is past-tense about a boot pass and whose second half is a structured `meta` record the CLI text face has no channel for. The per-finding lines are the shipped formatter's; the count heading is the command's own framing, exactly as the nav half leaves its heading to the commands.

The artifact package-id rule is imported too (`artifactPackages`), not re-spelled — that module's own header records why a second copy must not happen.

## Bounds the check keeps

- **Only the composed case is judged.** A name owned by a package installed from some OTHER artifact is invisible without a database, and guessing would report a package's own re-seed as a collision.
- **A package re-declaring its own set name is not a collision** — that is an idempotent re-seed at runtime, which is why the check asks the shipped ownership predicate rather than counting duplicate names.
- **A declaration with no resolvable owner is dropped, never reported** — the seeder returns at `if (!packageId)` with a different warning and never reaches the collision branch.
- The top-level `permissions` collection is read only when the stack carries no `packages[]`: `permissions` composes by `concat`, so on an artifact the top level is the union of every package's sets with per-package provenance flattened away.

## Verification

Build closure first, then every verdict:

| what | command | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| dependency closure | `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build` | exit 0 |
| type check | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`) |
| unit tier | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit` | 211 files / 3003 tests, 2974 passed, 29 skipped, 0 failed |
| new suite | `vitest run src/utils/permission-set-name-collisions.test.ts` | 10 passed (10) |
| derived gate families | `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` | **63 derived / 63 run / 0 NOT-MEASURED / 0 UNRUN** — reconciled with `--ran`, every line carrying its own exit code so the zero is DERIVED, not claimed |
| repo-wide lint | `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) | exit 0, no output |

`pnpm lint`, the 63-command gate sweep, the type check and the two touched suites (`permission-set-name-collisions.test.ts` + `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts`, 23 passed) were all run on this branch's final commit `20418d251` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), clean worktree. The dependency-closure build, the full unit tier and the ablation were run on `76a1ff09f`, whose tree differs from the final one only by the added changeset and the two commits `origin/main` brought in (`.claude/skills/**` and `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs`) — no package source among them, so none can move a TypeScript or vitest verdict.

Three of the 63 gate commands did not return 0 on their first run, and each was resolved rather than recorded as a pass:

- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n-coverage` both exited **3** — `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, naming packages with no `dist/`. ⛔ Not a pass and not a finding. After `pnpm build` (73 tasks, 72 cached) both re-ran to exit 0: 104 require entry points across 67 packages load; 13 i18n configs, 621 baselined untranslated strings, none new.
- `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` exits **1**, rooted in `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` — pre-existing on any tree with `packages/spec/dist` built, already filed as #18353 / #18348, untouched by this diff.

Two files in the unit tier first reported `packages/cli is not built (./dist/index.js is absent)` — a PREREQUISITE, not a verdict. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build` then re-running them: 2 files / 29 tests passed.

### Ablation — the pins FAIL on the wrong fix

Both legs mutated on disk, proven landed by `git hash-object` against the `HEAD` blob, run, restored, and the restore proven by hash equality plus a clean `git diff HEAD`. HEAD blob `dbf66ed`.

| leg | mutation | mutated | restored |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| baseline | — | — | 10 passed (10) |
| A | delete the `permissionSetNameIsForeign` call — i.e. the wrong fix, a name-duplicate counter | **1 failed** / 9 passed (`the SAME package declaring its own set name twice is NOT a collision`) | 10 passed (10), hash back to `dbf66ed` |
| B | stop walking `packages[]`, read the flattened top level instead | **5 failed** / 5 passed | 10 passed (10), hash back to `dbf66ed` |

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, not filed here

1. `packages/cli/src/utils/nav-contribution-groups.ts` exports `artifactPackagesOf`, a SECOND implementation of the artifact package-id rule that `packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts` owns, whose header says: *"⛔ A second copy is the one that must not happen… Two readers computing 'which package is this' slightly differently is how one entry comes to judge a different set of packages than the other while both look right."* The two already differ (the nav copy requires a non-empty `name` before falling back to it; `artifactPackages` does not). This change imports the owner rather than adding a third copy.
2. `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` says of its roster *"There is no third option — that is the whole point of the file"*, but its drift detector extracts only `lintFoo(` / `validateFoo(` call sites, so a `find*`-named gate is invisible to it: `findNavGroupDiagnostics` has been wired into both commands since #14553 and appears in no roster. This PR lists its own gate by name and records the blind spot in the roster's header; nav's row is left to whoever owns that card.
